Replacing Qt and Qt for Python Libraries in MyWB on macOS
=========================================================

MyWB uses Qt, PySide6, and shiboken6 through shared libraries. You may replace
the LGPL-covered libraries with modified, ABI-compatible versions for the
purpose of exercising rights granted by the LGPL. The MyWB license does not
prohibit reverse engineering when it is required by an applicable
third-party license.

These instructions apply to MyWB 0.4.0 for macOS arm64 and x86_64, built with
Qt 6.11.1 and Qt for Python 6.11.1. Later releases may use different paths or
versions.

1. Work on a copy
-----------------

Copy MyWB.app to a writable location. Keep the original copy so it can be
restored if an incompatible library prevents startup.

2. Obtain or build compatible libraries
---------------------------------------

Request the exact corresponding source under SOURCE-CODE-OFFER.txt, or use
another complete source copy for the same versions.

Build dynamic, ABI-compatible libraries for the architecture and minimum
macOS version identified by the MyWB release's About window and build
summary. Preserve the library install names expected by the application. The
Qt libraries in this release are loaded from:

MyWB.app/Contents/MacOS/

The PySide6 extension modules and Qt plugins are loaded from:

MyWB.app/Contents/MacOS/PySide6/

The shiboken6 extension module is loaded from:

MyWB.app/Contents/MacOS/shiboken6/

3. Replace the LGPL-covered files
---------------------------------

Replace only the corresponding Qt, PySide6, shiboken6, or plugin files in the
copied application bundle. Keep the same relative paths and filenames.

The Qt shared libraries use install names such as:

@executable_path/QtCore
@executable_path/QtGui
@executable_path/QtWidgets

If a replacement uses different install names, adjust the replacement with
Apple's install_name_tool or rebuild it with compatible install names.

4. Re-sign the modified local copy
----------------------------------

Replacing a library invalidates the original application signature. Sign the
modified files and application locally with an ad hoc signature. From
Terminal, with /path/to/MyWB.app replaced by the actual path, run:

codesign --force --deep --sign - /path/to/MyWB.app
codesign --verify --deep --strict --verbose=2 /path/to/MyWB.app

An ad hoc signature is sufficient for local testing. It does not recreate the
developer's notarized release signature.

5. Run and debug
----------------

Launch the modified local copy normally. If macOS reports a missing library,
inspect the replacement and its dependencies with:

otool -L /path/to/replacement-library

The replacement must remain ABI-compatible with the linked Qt for Python
extension modules. If PySide6 or shiboken6 is modified, replace the matching
set of binding libraries and extension modules together.

No MyWB application source code is required merely to replace the dynamically
linked LGPL-covered libraries. These instructions do not provide permission
to bypass MyWB Premium access controls; they apply to modification and
debugging of the LGPL-covered components.
